questions.prompt: What does the chapter mainly mean by calling religion a team sport?
choices: Religion is only a private belief system
Religion also binds people through shared practice and moral community
Religion is proven false by sociology

explanation.gentle: The phrase widens religion from private belief to shared social practice.
explanation.direct: The correct answer captures religion as organized group-binding life as well as doctrine.
explanation.competitive: The right pick sees religion running team machinery, not just storing beliefs.

questions.prompt: How does Chapter 11 build on Chapter 10?
choices: It abandons group-mindedness and returns to isolated reasoning
It asks which institutions can trigger and stabilize group-minded coordination repeatedly
It claims ritual has nothing to do with coordination

explanation.gentle: Chapter 10 explained the switch; Chapter 11 asks who can organize it durably.
explanation.direct: The chapter turns activated coordination into an institutional question.
explanation.competitive: The mechanism from Chapter 10 gets an operator here.

questions.prompt: Why do rituals and symbols matter in the team-sport framing?
choices: They help coordinate belonging, trust, and shared moral life
They are irrelevant compared with doctrine
They guarantee a group's moral purity

explanation.gentle: Rituals and symbols help make the group feel shared and morally real.
explanation.direct: The chapter treats them as tools for organizing coordinated community.
explanation.competitive: They are part of the gear that locks the team together.

questions.prompt: Students argue whether religion should be judged only by doctrine. Which chapter response fits best?
choices: Yes, because social practice adds nothing important
No, because religion also functions through ritual, obligation, and group binding
No, because the chapter proves all doctrine is meaningless

explanation.gentle: The chapter widens religion beyond doctrine without erasing doctrine.
explanation.direct: Its point is that religion has to be read socially as well as doctrinally.
explanation.competitive: The creed matters, but the team-binding machinery matters too.

questions.prompt: What warning does the chapter attach to religion's binding power?
choices: Strong belonging can also sharpen exclusion and certainty
Group binding automatically makes communities morally better
The social function makes truth questions irrelevant

explanation.gentle: The same power that creates meaning can also narrow concern for outsiders.
explanation.direct: Religious cohesion remains morally double-edged in the chapter.
explanation.competitive: The sacred glue can build the inside and harden the wall.

questions.prompt: Which mistake does the chapter avoid?
choices: Reducing religion to pure fraud or settling its truth-value outright
Connecting religion to social coordination
Linking the chapter to the hive switch

explanation.gentle: The chapter avoids flattening religion into a single dismissive story.
explanation.direct: It interprets religion through group function without pretending that solves every question.
explanation.competitive: The chapter refuses both cheap debunking and fake final verdicts.

questions.prompt: Why is religion especially important after the hive-switch chapter?
choices: Because it shows how intensified group-mindedness can be organized repeatedly
Because it removes the need for ritual
Because it proves disagreement is trivial

explanation.gentle: Religion becomes a major example of durable organized group binding.
explanation.direct: The chapter shows how an institution can repeatedly trigger and stabilize coordinated moral life.
explanation.competitive: Religion keeps the switch hot instead of letting it fade.

questions.prompt: If a community becomes more cohesive through sacred practices, what should a reader also check?
choices: Whether the practices automatically make the group right
Whether the same cohesion is narrowing criticism or outsider concern
Whether doctrine no longer matters at all

explanation.gentle: The chapter says belonging gains and narrowing risks need to be read together.
explanation.direct: Readers should check for boundary-hardening alongside stronger solidarity.
explanation.competitive: Whenever the sacred glue works, ask what wall it is building too.

questions.prompt: What larger synthesis does Chapter 11 provide for Part III?
choices: It drops the earlier framework and starts over
It gives the strongest institutional example of binding and blinding together
It proves moral conflict is only about facts

explanation.gentle: The chapter shows a durable human system for organizing the forces Part III has been tracing.
explanation.direct: Religion becomes the clearest institutional payoff of groupishness and the hive switch.
explanation.competitive: This is where the machinery gets its strongest real-world operator.

questions.prompt: Why does Chapter 11 prepare the final chapter on disagreement?
choices: Because once religion is read socially, conflict looks like a clash of moral communities as well as ideas
Because the book is now promising consensus
Because politics and religion no longer matter

explanation.gentle: The chapter makes disagreement look deeper than a simple exchange of claims.
explanation.direct: Readers can approach the final chapter with a better grasp of the social worlds people defend.
explanation.competitive: The last fights get heavier once you see people defending whole moral teams.
